import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Class number problem for real quadratic fields

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_number_problem)
-/
open Polynomial
namespace ClassNumberProblem

def IsClassNumberOne (d : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h₂ : Irreducible (X ^ 2 - C (d : ℚ))),
  have := Fact.mk h₂
  NumberField.classNumber (AdjoinRoot (X ^ 2 - C (d : ℚ))) = 1

/--
There are infinitely many real quadratic fields `ℚ(√d)` with class number one,
where `d > 1` is a squarefree integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem class_number_problem :
    { d : ℤ | Squarefree d ∧ d > 1 ∧ IsClassNumberOne d }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
**Stark–Heegner theorem** : For any squarefree integer `d < 0`, the class number of the imaginary
quadratic field Q(√d) is one if and only if `d ∈ {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163}`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem class_number_problem.variants.imaginary :
    { d : ℤ | Squarefree d ∧ d < 0 ∧ IsClassNumberOne d } =
    {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163} := by
  sorry

end ClassNumberProblem

reformulations.difference: The predicate existentially packages a proof that X² − d is irreducible before asserting class number one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Irreducibility is automatic on both theorem domains: a squarefree integer other than 1 cannot be a rational square, and a negative integer cannot be a rational square. The witness supplies the standard field and number-field instances on ℚ[X]/(X² − d); proof irrelevance makes its choice immaterial. In scratch.lean I proved irreducibility on both domains and the equivalence between IsClassNumberOne d and the class-number equality using any fixed irreducibility proof. I also proved equivalence with the full ring of integers being a PID. Thus this existential adds no restriction or vacuity to either statement.

reformulations.difference: Infinitude is stated for squarefree integer radicands d > 1 rather than for isomorphism classes of real quadratic fields.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every real quadratic field is ℚ(√d) for a unique squarefree integer d > 1. For injectivity, an isomorphism between ℚ(√d) and ℚ(√e) forces d/e to be a rational square; squarefreeness and positivity then give d = e. Field isomorphisms preserve the ring of integers and its class number. Consequently the parameter set is infinite exactly when there are infinitely many real quadratic fields of class number one.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_number_problem — especially “Gauss's original conjectures”, “Status”, “Modern developments”, and “Real quadratic fields”.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_field — unique squarefree-radicand parameterization and the field-discriminant formula.
H. M. Stark, “The Gauss Class-Number Problems”, Clay Mathematics Proceedings 7 (2007), pp. 247–256, https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/cmip07c.pdf.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The imaginary theorem gives exactly the source's nine squarefree radicands; these should not be confused with its separate fundamental-discriminant list. Its set equality was proved equivalent to the docstring's pointwise biconditional in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Boundary checks confirm that −1 is squarefree and admissible, all nine listed radicands are negative and squarefree, and square radicands such as 0, 1, 4, and 9 cannot satisfy the helper. Mathlib's classNumber counts the finite ordinary ideal class group of the full ring of integers, not the class group of ℤ[√d] or of the field itself. The scratch file compiles cleanly, and the checked equivalences have no sorryAx dependency. The source still records the real problem as open and the imaginary classification as solved, agreeing with both category tags.
